newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CONINE STROKES GAME-WINNING HOMER IN NINTH FOR MARLINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CONINE STROKES GAME-WINNING HOMER IN NINTH FOR MARLINS.

text.p: Jeff Conine shook off flu symptoms that kept him out of the starting lineup to deliver a pinch-hit home run in the bottom of the ninth inning that lifted the Florida Marlins to a 2-1 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Thursday.
"I don't think there is a greater feeling in all of sports than a home run in that situation," Conine said.

Mark Petkovsek (1-2) replaced starter Todd Stottlemyre to start the ninth for Florida. Conine got hold of a a high forkball from Petkovsek and laced a fly ball down the left-field line that curved just inside the foul pole for his third homer of the year.
"I don't like sitting on the bench. I like playing," Conine said. "This morning I was thinking more about running to the bathroom than running to first base."
Mark Hutton (1-1) was the winner, pitching two scoreless innings in relief of Kevin Brown.
Florida had tied the game with a run in the eighth on Edgar Renteria's RBI single that scored Devon White, who stole second to get into scoring position.

Rookie catcher Mike DiFelice stole home in third for the lone St. Louis run. He delivered a leadoff double and went to third on a passed ball by Gregg Zaun. Correctly anticipating a squeeze play, the Marlins called for a pitchout, but Zaun momentarily bobbled the pitch from Brown and DiFelice slid home safely.
In Pittsburgh, Jermaine Allensworth delivered a bases-clearing double in the fifth and Esteban Loaiza allowed one run over seven innings to lead Pirates to a 3-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.

Reds starter Mike Morgan (0-1) carried a 1-0 lead into the fifth, but the Pirates loaded the bases on a single and two walks. Allensworth then ripped a 1-0 pitch down the left-field line to drive home all three Pittsburgh runs.
Morgan lasted 4 2/3 innings, taking the loss despite giving up just two hits. Loaiza (2-0) limited Cincinnati to six hits with one walk and seven strikeouts.
Closer John Ericks entered the game with two out in the ninth and got himself into and out of a jam to record his fifth save as the Reds lost their fourth in a row and ninth in 11 games.
Ericks has figured in all six Pittsburgh victories with one win and five saves.
